id.description: The relation id, snake_case, documented on the methodology page of the method.

pointer.description:
JSON pointer of the result block the check belongs to, from the root of the result
envelope, for example `/value/years/0`.

pointers.description:
JSON pointers of the inputs on both sides of the relation, from the root of the input
sent, as read; empty when the sides are computed outputs.

CheckStatus.description:
The status of a relation. Values may be added, never renamed (ADR 0014 G8). A relation that
fails is an error (`FM-E026`), never a check.

oneOf.description: Both sides given and equal.
A side is missing: the relation could not be checked.

DefaultApplied.description:
A documented default filled in because the field was not given (SPEC-0001 R31). Listed in
`meta.defaults_applied` and reported as a convention starting with "default:".

pointer.description:
JSON pointer of the field filled in, for example `/timing` or `/stages/0/periods`, or of
the item given whose default destination applies, from the root of the input sent.

reason.description: Why this value: one line, citing the practice or the rule it follows.

value.description: The value filled in, as it would be written in the input.

Diagnostics.description:
What the result does not contain, what the reader could miss and what was verified (ADR
0014 G4). Every list is always present, empty when there is nothing to report.

checks.description:
Every relation the method verified or could not verify, ordered by result block, then by
`id`; empty for a method without checks.

not_computed.description:
The outputs not computed, one entry per output, ordered by `pointer` (array indices
compared as numbers); empty when every output is computed.

warnings.description:
The warnings of the catalogue (`docs/en/reference/warnings.md`), in the order of their
echo in `explain.conventions`; empty when nothing is warned.

conventions.description:
Conventions applied (timing, discounting of the terminal value, ...), the documented
defaults (`default: ...`) and the echo of every warning (`warning FM-Wnnn: ...`).

formula.description: The method's formula in plain notation.

FairmarkErrorEntry.description:
One error of a report (ADR 0014 G5): the stable code, the message in English, and what a
client needs to correct the input without reading the message.

code.description: Stable error code, for example `FM-E004` (see the errors reference).

expected.description:
What the field accepts. With `reason` `enum` or `unknown_field`, the literal values
(the values of the enumeration, the fields of the object); with any other reason, short
descriptions of the accepted form, for example "an amount greater than 0". Empty when
not known.

fix.description:
One sentence that resolves the error; `null` when the message is the only guidance.
Its wording may change between releases; `code`, `pointer` and `reason` do not.

message.description: What is wrong and, where known, how to fix it.

missing_any_of.description:
`FM-E027` only: alternative sets of input pointers, any one of which lifts the input
above the minimum of the method. Omitted for every other code.

pointer.description:
JSON pointer (RFC 6901) of the field to correct, always from the root of the input the
client sent: an error of the method evaluated by an analysis is under `/base_input`,
while its message keeps the pointer within `base_input`. `null` only for a text that is
not JSON (`reason` `syntax`) and for an error raised during the computation that no
single field causes (and for `FM-E027`, which names its inputs in `missing_any_of`).

pointers.description:
JSON pointers of every field of a relation (both sides of an `FM-E026`
reconciliation, both fields of a conflict); empty when the error concerns one field.

reason.description:
The sub-kind of the error, which tells apart the conditions that share a code; `null`
when the code has one meaning only.

FairmarkErrorReason.description:
The sub-kind of an error (ADR 0014 G5): it tells apart the conditions that share a code,
above all `FM-E001`, without new codes. Values are added, never renamed or removed; a
client accepts a value it does not know.

oneOf.description:
The text is not JSON (a syntax error, a truncated input, trailing characters): there
is no field to name, and the message keeps the line and column.
A required field, or one required by the other fields given, is absent.
A field the input does not define.
A field given twice in the same object.

A value of the wrong type: a text where a number is expected, an object where a list
is expected, a date that is not a calendar date.
A value outside a closed list of values; `expected` lists them.
Fields that exclude each other are given together, or contradict each other.
A field is given without the field it needs, or is not used by the choice made.
An amount with the wrong sign for its field.
A text that must say something is empty or blank.
A number outside the domain of its field.

A list with the wrong number of entries: empty, too long, or not one entry per period
or year.
Two sides of a relation that must agree differ: a total and its parts (`FM-E026`).

FairmarkErrorReport.description: The report of an error (ADR 0014 G5): the first error found, and every error found.

code.description: Stable error code, for example `FM-E004` (see the errors reference).

errors.description:
Every error found, at least one, the first equal to the top level: the validation of
the input reports all the errors it finds, in the order of its checks; an error raised
during the computation stops it and is the only entry.

expected.description:
What the field accepts. With `reason` `enum` or `unknown_field`, the literal values
(the values of the enumeration, the fields of the object); with any other reason, short
descriptions of the accepted form, for example "an amount greater than 0". Empty when
not known.

fix.description:
One sentence that resolves the error; `null` when the message is the only guidance.
Its wording may change between releases; `code`, `pointer` and `reason` do not.

message.description: What is wrong and, where known, how to fix it.

missing_any_of.description:
`FM-E027` only: alternative sets of input pointers, any one of which lifts the input
above the minimum of the method. Omitted for every other code.

pointer.description:
JSON pointer (RFC 6901) of the field to correct, always from the root of the input the
client sent: an error of the method evaluated by an analysis is under `/base_input`,
while its message keeps the pointer within `base_input`. `null` only for a text that is
not JSON (`reason` `syntax`) and for an error raised during the computation that no
single field causes (and for `FM-E027`, which names its inputs in `missing_any_of`).

pointers.description:
JSON pointers of every field of a relation (both sides of an `FM-E026`
reconciliation, both fields of a conflict); empty when the error concerns one field.

reason.description:
The sub-kind of the error, which tells apart the conditions that share a code; `null`
when the code has one meaning only.

FairmarkErrorResponse.description: What an adapter returns when a method fails: `{"error": <report>}`.
FairmarkErrorResponse.title: FairmarkErrorResponse

Meta.description: Reproducibility metadata attached to every result.

defaults_applied.description:
Documented defaults filled in because their fields were not given, in input order;
empty when none applies.

engine_version.description: Version of the fairmark engine that produced the result.

envelope_version.description:
Version of the envelope, an integer: 1 for `{method, value, explain, diagnostics,
meta}` (ADR 0014 G4).

evaluated_method_status.description: Analysis methods only: status of the method they evaluated (ADR 0012).

input_hash.description:
SHA-256 of the canonical input, with the documented defaults filled in: same hash +
same versions = same value.

method_status.description: Status of the method that produced the result, `available` or `preview` (ADR 0012).

method_version.description: Version of the method implementation. Bumped on any numerical change.

NotComputed.description: An output not computed, and why.

missing_any_of.description:
Alternative sets of input pointers, from the root of the input sent: any one set given
makes the output computable. Empty for `not_defined` and `not_applicable`.

permitted.description: The choices to make for `choice_required`; empty otherwise.

pointer.description: JSON pointer of the output, from the root of the result envelope (`/value/...`).

reason.description: The reason in one sentence, in English; guidance, not contract.

Permitted.description: A choice the analyst must make for an output to be computed.

pointer.description: JSON pointer of the input to give, from the root of the input sent.

ReasonCode.description: Why an output is not computed. Values may be added, never renamed (ADR 0014 G8).

oneOf.description:
An input it needs is not given; `missing_any_of` lists the inputs that make it
computable.
A treatment or a choice must be given; `permitted` lists the values to choose from.
A given term makes the output not defined, for example a ratio over a negative equity.

No input could supply it in the form given, for example a statutory output of an entry
given in reclassified form.

Status.description:
How far a method has been verified (ADR 0012). Defined, with the promotion rule, in
`docs/en/project/releases.md`; both statuses follow the versioning rules of ADR 0009.

oneOf.description: Meets the promotion rule: approved spec, independent audit and review recorded.
Implemented, tested and documented, not yet promoted: tell users so.

Step.description: One auditable step of a calculation.

formula.description: The formula with the actual numbers substituted.

label.description: Human-readable label, e.g. "Present value of FCF, year 3".

value.description: The exact decimal result of this step.

Warning.description: A condition the reader could miss (ADR 0014 G4).

code.description: The code of the condition, documented in `docs/en/reference/warnings.md`.

message.description: The warning in one sentence, in English; guidance, not contract.

pointer.description:
JSON pointer of the field the warning concerns, from the root its catalogue entry states:
the input sent, or the result envelope when it starts with `/value`; null only where the
catalogue entry says so.

WarningCode.description: The code of a warning: FM-W and three digits, documented in docs/en/reference/warnings.md, never reused or renumbered. Clients accept codes they do not know.

description:
The envelope every method returns (ADR 0014 G4). Its JSON Schema, with `value` described by
the method's output schema, is `registry::result_schema`.

diagnostics.description: What the result does not contain, what the reader could miss and what was verified.

explain.description: How the result was obtained: formula, steps and conventions.

meta.description:
Reproducibility metadata: engine, envelope and method versions, status, input hash,
defaults.

method.description: Id of the method that produced the result, for example `dcf.fcff`.

value.description: The method's output, described by schemas/<method>/v<N>.output.json for the method and version named by `method` and `meta.method_version`.
